subject: Route sampling, cost attribution and ownership — console observability ask

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: Route sampling, cost attribution and ownership — console observability ask

Team —

Quick request from AE/CS: GridWorks is asking for more control and visibility over per-route cost and tail-latency sampling. Their ask has three parts and they want to know whether we can surface this in the Redwood Console (and what the roadmap/ETA looks like):

1) Per-route cost attribution: a dashboard filter to attribute token and GPU cost back to a route (and optionally a customer tag) for the last 7/30/90 days.
2) Route-level sampling controls: ability to set sampling rates (e.g., 1%, 5%, 100%) per-route to capture full traces/inputs for QA and regression monitoring without incurring full storage costs.
3) Ownership + alerting: map a route to an owning team/person and enable per-route budget alerts / anomaly detection so customers can cap runaway costs.

Why this matters: GridWorks has an upcoming procurement review and needs to show SOC+ cost controls to their finance team. They also run a lot of experiment routes (canaries) and want a cheap way to sample and trace regressions.

Questions for product/infra:
- Feasibility and a recommended phased approach (what can we do quick vs. needs infra changes)
- Rough ETA and engineering effort (ballpark sprints)
- Any storage/cost SLO tradeoffs we should call out to the customer

I attached a screenshot of the current Route Explorer they referenced (current-route-explorer.png). Can we try to land a short proposal this week so I can share back with GridWorks?

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 9:12 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick request from AE/CS: GridWorks is asking for more control and visibility over per-route cost and tail-latency sampling.

Thanks for the context, Dylan — this is something we've been getting more frequently. A couple of clarifying Qs before Marcus and I sketch a phased approach:

- Cardinality: how many unique routes does GridWorks run at peak? (are we talking dozens, hundreds, thousands?)
- Attribution scope: do they need token-level dollar attribution (precise cost) or an estimate by percent split?
- Sampling retention: how long do they want sampled payloads retained (30/90/365 days)?

High-level proposal (two-phase):
Phase 1 (Q1): add a per-route cost breakdown that ties to existing billing aggregates + basic tagging UI to assign "owner" and budget cap. Expose exportable CSVs and per-route alert thresholds.
Phase 2 (Q2+): sampling controls in the console (sample rate selector per-route), sampled payload storage with TTL, and integrations for alerts (PagerDuty/Slack).

I'll attach the current obs roadmap snapshot (obs-roadmap-snapshot.pdf) — I'll try to pencil this into early Q1 but want Marcus to weigh in on infra cost.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Lead, Observability

Subject: Re: Route sampling, cost attribution and ownership — console observability ask

Thanks — putting some technical constraints on the table so expectations are aligned.

Feasibility notes:
- Per-route cost attribution: doable by enriching our token accounting pipeline with route_id tagging. If we maintain a mapping from route->customer, we can roll up cost with existing aggregation jobs. The challenge is cardinality: supporting thousands of high-card routes will increase storage and aggregation CPU.
- Sampling controls: UI-side is straightforward. Backend requires a sampling hook in the serving runtime that emits sampled traces to an events pipeline with configurable rate. We'll need to add rate-limited ingress and TTL-based retention in object storage.
- Ownership & alerting: metadata layer + alerting rules are straightforward; linking to budgeted alerts requires periodic cost rollups (hourly) and alert evaluation.

Estimated effort (rough):
- MVP per-route cost breakdown: 3 sprints (1 infra, 1 aggregation, 1 UI)
- Sampling controls + storage retention (MVP): 4 sprints (runtime + pipeline + storage + UI)
- Add anomaly detection/alerts: 2 sprints

Operational tradeoffs:
- If we enable 100% sampling for many routes this could increase S3/ingress costs ~5–12% depending on sample size.
- We should default sample rate to 1% and provide clear billing guidance in console when customers raise it.

I'll create a backlog ticket and link SUP-4821 here; Marcus will own infra changes. Grace — if you can confirm priority I can scope the JIRA properly.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Quick note from CS/Customer side: GridWorks (Amelia Park, product lead) confirmed they run ~120 active routes and would be comfortable with a 1% default sampling model as long as they can toggle up to 5–10% for canaries. They also want per-route budget alerts routed to Finance and a weekly export for auditing.

Procurement timeline: they have a cost review on 2026-12-15 and asked for PRD/ETA by 2026-12-08. If we can't promise a shipped timeline, they may request a commercial credit for interim monitoring.

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below so I can respond back to GridWorks by EOD Friday: 

Summary:
- Scope: Per-route cost rollups (MVP: estimated cost by route, exportable CSV) + route owner tags + sampling controls (default 1%, up to 10% per-route) + per-route budget alerts.
- Effort: Marcus estimates ~3 sprints for the cost view, ~4 sprints for sampling plumbing, + 2 sprints for alerts; could be parallelized.
- Risk: sampling retention increases storage costs; recommend default 1% with console warnings.

Action items & owners:
- SUP-4821 (backlog ticket) — Marcus Lin (infra owner)
- Roadmap prioritization — Grace O'Connor (product) to slot early-Q1 if possible
- Customer comms & procurement ask — Neha to confirm exact export cadence and whether they need a formal credit if timeline slips
- Draft PRD + high-level ETA for GridWorks by 2026-12-08 — Dylan to consolidate and send to Amelia

I'll set up a 30-min sync (invite incoming) for Thurs to walk through the proposed MVP and the JIRA acceptance criteria. If you have any objections to the owners above speak up now.

Thanks,
Dylan
